### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>dateutil/dateutil (python-dateutil)</summary>

### [`v4.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/releases/tag/4.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/compare/3.0.0...4.0.0)

`dateutil` 4.0 requires Python 3.11 or later and no longer depends on `six`. Apart from that, the changes in this release are bug fixes, but note that `isoparse` is now stricter about the numeric fields it accepts (see below).

#### Deprecations

- Dropped support for Python versions older than 3.11 and removed the dependency on `six`, along with Python 2 compatibility helpers that were never part of the public API, such as `dateutil.tz.tzname_in_python2`. (gh pr [#​1625](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1625))

#### Bugfixes

- `parser.isoparse`, and the `isoparser` methods `parse_isodate`, `parse_isotime` and `parse_tzstr`, now require each numeric field to be exactly the expected number of ASCII digits. Strings that were previously accepted, such as `20200728121240` (read as 21:24), `2014- 4-21` and `2_14-04-21`, and offsets such as `+-1:00`, now raise `ValueError`. `tzical` applies the same check to `TZOFFSETFROM` and `TZOFFSETTO`. Reported by [@​janos-gonye](https://redirect.github.com/janos-gonye) (gh issue [#​1074](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1074)). Fixed by [@​varun3257](https://redirect.github.com/varun3257) (gh pr [#​1617](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1617)).
- Fixed an issue where iterating over a cached `rrule` or `rruleset` could hang forever if another iterator over the same rule had already completed the cache, for example when a cached `rrule` was included twice in an `rruleset`. Reported by [@​bysiber](https://redirect.github.com/bysiber) (gh pr [#​1455](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1455)). Fixed by [@​pganssle](https://redirect.github.com/pganssle) (gh pr [#​1655](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1655)).
- Unpickling a `tzutc` now gives the `dateutil.tz.UTC` singleton, and unpickling a `tzoffset` gives the same object as calling `tzoffset(name, offset)`. Previously unpickling bypassed the singleton-generation logic. Reported and fixed by [@​masipcat](https://redirect.github.com/masipcat) (gh issue [#​1051](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1051), gh pr [#​1053](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1053)).
- `relativedelta(yearday=366)` now resolves to December 31 in leap years. Previously it gave December 30, the same date as `yearday=365`. Reported and fixed by [@​Master-Norna](https://redirect.github.com/Master-Norna) (gh pr [#​1583](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1583)).

#### Misc

- The build backend is now Hatchling, and the package metadata is in `pyproject.toml`. Versions are still derived from Git tags and exposed as `dateutil.__version__`. This mainly affects people building `dateutil` from source. (gh pr [#​1637](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1637), [#​1638](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1638))
- Changes to CI, tests and release tooling that do not affect users of the package: gh pr [#​1636](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1636), [#​1644](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1644), [#​1645](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1645), [#​1646](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1646), [#​1648](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1648), [#​1649](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1649), [#​1650](https://redirect.github.com/dateutil/dateutil/issues/1650).

</details>
